# Spec: docs-front-door
<!-- Generated by /hefesto:hef.spec -->
<!-- Date: 2026-11-07 -->
<!-- Board item: HEF-18 -->

## Overview

The docs are a reference, not a front door. `README.md` is 415 lines of edge cases; installing,
setting up and using hefesto are spread over `README.md`, `docs/quickstart.md`, `docs/install.md` and
`SETUP.md` with no single "start here"; there is no contributing guide; the OS differences are scattered
sentences (Windows/WSL is not mentioned at all); and the single-lane versus four-lane choice is a small
table in the quick start.

This feature restructures the documentation so a newcomer reads, in order: **what hefesto is → how to
install it → how to set a project up → how to use it → how to contribute**. It is a documentation-only
change plus the smoke guards that pin the docs; no hook, command, helper or `install.sh` behaviour
changes.

### Decisions taken here (decided from the code, not open questions)

- **File layout — flat under `docs/`.** The new pages are `docs/install-linux.md`,
  `docs/install-macos.md`, `docs/install-windows.md` and `docs/contributing.md`. Flat, not a
  `docs/install/` folder, because the smoke guards that keep docs honest (relative links resolve,
  no `$HOME`/`~` permission rule in a fenced block, no dead `stow claude` install,
  `tests/smoke.sh:396,411,435`) iterate `README.md` and `docs/*.md` only; a nested page or a root
  `CONTRIBUTING.md` would silently escape them.
- **One job per file:**

  | File | Its one job |
  |---|---|
  | `README.md` | Front door: what it is, install in one command, setup, first use, the two approaches and how to choose, contribute, links. |
  | `docs/install-linux.md` / `-macos.md` / `-windows.md` | Installing on that OS: the prerequisite tools, the one install command, the check. The only place the quick install steps live. |
  | `docs/quickstart.md` (+ `.pt-BR.md`) | After the install: prepare the project, single lane or four lanes, day to day, upgrade notes. |
  | `docs/install.md` | The install & configuration **reference**: manual install, profiles, optional configuration, sandbox, updating, what the plugin cannot ship, the orchestrator (§7). |
  | `SETUP.md` | The runbook Claude follows. Its steps and behaviour are unchanged; only its pointers to other docs are updated. |
  | `docs/contributing.md` | How to change hefesto itself: the smoke suite, commit and PR conventions, how a change is reviewed. |

- **`docs/install.md` keeps its section numbers (§1–§7).** Code and messages cite them by number:
  `docs/install.md §7` (`hooks/status-board.sh:307`, `hooks/board-lib.sh:18`,
  `hooks/session-start-context.sh:171`, `tests/smoke.sh:4102`), `§5` (`install.sh:973`), `§14`
  (`hooks/board-github.sh:218`). §1 becomes a short pointer to the per-OS pages plus the manual,
  multi-profile and naming material, so nothing after it renumbers.
- **The quick start keeps its six numbered sections.** The guard at `tests/smoke.sh:6011-6024` requires
  exactly six `## N.` sections and 3–5 steps in sections 5 and 6. Sections 1 ("Before you start") and 2
  ("Install or upgrade") become short hand-overs to the per-OS pages; the per-OS tool commands
  (`bubblewrap`, `brew install`) move to those pages, and the guard is updated to require them there and
  to require the quick start to link the three pages.
- **Windows is WSL 2.** hefesto's hooks, helpers and `install.sh` are bash and assume a POSIX userland
  (`install.sh:446` distinguishes only Darwin from everything else); there is no native-Windows path. The
  Windows page says WSL is required, names WSL 2 (Claude Code's sandbox uses `bubblewrap`, which needs the
  WSL 2 kernel), and hands over to the Linux page for every step after WSL is installed.
- **Per-OS pages are English only.** The Portuguese quick start links them, the same way it already links
  the English `install.md`. Keeping the Portuguese quick start "in step" means: same six sections, same
  hand-overs, same links, same commands.
- **No fact is lost.** Every statement removed from `README.md` either already exists in a `docs/` page or
  moves to one; the plan lists each README section and its destination. Moved text is not rewritten beyond
  what the move needs.
- **Guarded README strings stay.** The README must keep: the version footer that `hooks/release.sh:38`
  rewrites and `tests/smoke.sh:116` reads (`**Framework Version**: X.Y.Z … **Last Updated**: YYYY-MM-DD`);
  the counts `27 \`hef.*\` commands`, `sixteen hooks` and `(46 subcommands)` (`tests/smoke.sh:2483-2485`,
  values computed from the tree at implement time); the phrase `fresh context` (`tests/smoke.sh:1912`);
  and `/hefesto:hef.babysit` (`tests/smoke.sh:2883`).
- **The install wizard is not touched.** `install.sh` already prints links to `docs/quickstart.md` /
  `docs/quickstart.pt-BR.md` and `docs/install.md` (`tests/smoke.sh:4383,4507`); both files keep existing.

## User Scenarios

### US1: A newcomer reads the README front door [P1]
- **Given** a person who has never used hefesto opens `README.md`
- **When** they read it top to bottom
- **Then** they meet, in this order, what hefesto is, the one install command with a link to their OS's
  page, how to set a project up, a first use, the single-lane and four-or-more-lane approaches with how to
  choose, how to contribute, and links to the rest of the docs — in under 150 lines
- **Edge:** a reader who wants a detail the README dropped (the hooks list, the pane tables, the command
  table) finds a link to the `docs/` page that holds it
- **Error / must NOT happen:** the README must not drop a string a smoke guard or `hooks/release.sh` reads,
  must not spell a command other than `/hefesto:hef.<name>`, and must not link a file that does not exist
- Touches: `README.md`; tests: `tests/smoke.sh` (doc counts, footer, links, command spelling)

### US2: A person installs on their OS from one page [P1]
- **Given** a person on Linux (Ubuntu/Debian, Fedora, Arch), macOS, or Windows
- **When** they open the install page for their OS
- **Then** it lists the prerequisite tools with that OS's install command, the one install command
  (`bash <(curl -fsSL …/install.sh)`), what the wizard does and its options, and how to check the install
  (`/hefesto:hef.doctor`); then hands over to the quick start
- **Edge:** on Windows the page says WSL is required, shows how to get WSL 2 and a Linux distribution, and
  sends the reader to the Linux page for everything after that, without repeating the Linux steps
- **Error / must NOT happen:** the per-OS tool commands and the quick install steps are not repeated in
  `README.md`, `docs/quickstart.md`, `docs/quickstart.pt-BR.md` or `docs/install.md` (those link the pages);
  no page claims a native-Windows install works
- Touches: `docs/install-linux.md`, `docs/install-macos.md`, `docs/install-windows.md`; tests:
  `tests/smoke.sh` (quick-start guard, links)

### US3: Each install/setup document has one job and points to the others [P1]
- **Given** `docs/quickstart.md`, `docs/install.md` and `SETUP.md` overlap today
- **When** a reader opens any one of them
- **Then** its opening says what that document is for and links the other two (and the per-OS pages) for
  what it is not for
- **Edge:** a link or message that cites `docs/install.md §N` still lands on the same section
- **Error / must NOT happen:** `SETUP.md` changes no step, check, command or rule Claude follows (only its
  pointers change); `docs/install.md` loses no section a guard requires (`--stage`,
  `/hefesto:hef.babysit`, `CLAUDE_CODE_TMPDIR`, `External board`, `/sandbox`, the lifecycle words in
  `tests/smoke-lifecycle-ops.sh:220`)
- Touches: `docs/quickstart.md`, `docs/install.md`, `SETUP.md`; tests: `tests/smoke.sh`,
  `tests/smoke-lifecycle-ops.sh`

### US4: A contributor finds how to change hefesto [P1]
- **Given** a person wants to change hefesto itself
- **When** they follow the README's "Contribute" link
- **Then** `docs/contributing.md` tells them how to run the smoke suite (`tests/smoke.sh`, the live tier
  with `SMOKE_LIVE=1`, `node --test` for `workflows/`), the commit convention (a conventional subject,
  enforced by the commit hook `hooks/quality-before-commit.sh:66-69`; the co-author trailer, a
  `.claude/rules/git-workflow.md` convention the hook does not check), the branch names, the merge
  convention (merge commits, never squash or rebase — the `human:merge` gate is an ancestry check,
  `docs/install.md` §7 step 2), and how a change is reviewed (`/hefesto:hef.review` code mode
  through a fresh-context reviewer, CI `smoke` + `smoke-macos`, a person merges)
- **Edge:** a contributor without the `claude` CLI logged in can still run tier 1 (the end-to-end check
  self-skips)
- **Error / must NOT happen:** the guide states nothing the repo does not do (every convention cited from
  `.claude/rules/git-workflow.md`, `.github/workflows/smoke.yml`, `hooks/` or the constitution) and names no
  adopting project (hefesto is project-agnostic)
- Touches: `docs/contributing.md`, `README.md`

### US5: The single-lane vs four-or-more-lane choice is explicit [P2]
- **Given** a person who has installed hefesto
- **When** they reach the README's approaches section or quick start §3
- **Then** they see both approaches (single lane; four or more lanes — four, plus extra builders with
  `orchestrate.max_builders`) and a short rule for choosing, with the quick start sections that run each
- **Error / must NOT happen:** the README and the quick start do not contradict each other on the setup
  command (`hefesto-setup.sh` vs `hefesto-setup.sh --lanes`)
- Touches: `README.md`, `docs/quickstart.md`, `docs/quickstart.pt-BR.md`

### US6: The Portuguese quick start stays in step [P2]
- **Given** the English quick start changed
- **When** a Portuguese reader opens `docs/quickstart.pt-BR.md`
- **Then** it has the same six sections, the same hand-overs to the per-OS pages, the same links and the
  same commands
- **Error / must NOT happen:** a link, command or section present in one and missing from the other
- Touches: `docs/quickstart.pt-BR.md`; tests: `tests/smoke.sh:6011` loop (both files)

## Functional Requirements

| ID | Requirement | Priority | Scenario |
|----|-------------|----------|----------|
| FR-001 | `README.md` is under 150 lines and its sections appear in this order: what it is, install, setup, first use, the two approaches and how to choose, contribute, links (docs table), then license and the version footer. | P1 | US1 |
| FR-002 | `README.md` keeps every string a guard or tool reads: the release footer, `<N> \`hef.*\` commands`, `<words> hooks`, `(<N> subcommands)`, `fresh context`, `/hefesto:hef.babysit`; values match the tree. | P1 | US1 |
| FR-003 | Every README section removed or shortened has a destination in `docs/` that already holds or now holds its facts; the plan records the mapping and nothing is dropped. | P1 | US1 |
| FR-004 | `docs/install-linux.md` lists the tools per distribution (Ubuntu/Debian, Fedora, Arch: `git jq bubblewrap socat`, `gh`), the one install command, the wizard's behaviour and options, `gh auth login`, and the check with `/hefesto:hef.doctor`; it ends with a link to the quick start. | P1 | US2 |
| FR-005 | `docs/install-macos.md` does the same for macOS (`xcode-select --install`, `brew install jq gh`, the sandbox is built in, stock `/bin/bash` 3.2 suffices). | P1 | US2 |
| FR-006 | `docs/install-windows.md` says WSL (WSL 2) is required and native Windows is not supported, shows how to install WSL 2 with a Linux distribution, says to run everything inside the WSL terminal, and hands over to `install-linux.md` without repeating its steps. | P1 | US2 |
| FR-007 | The per-OS tool commands and the quick install walkthrough appear only on the per-OS pages; `README.md`, both quick starts and `docs/install.md` link the pages instead (the README keeps the one install command line; each quick start keeps one sentence naming `install.sh` as the install-and-upgrade command, without the curl line or the walkthrough; `docs/install.md` §1 keeps the wizard's full option reference as its single owner). The Linux and macOS pages' §2 also carry the two other install forms the README and `docs/install.md:14` hold today: the pinned-tag URL (`…/v<X.Y.Z>/install.sh`, 7.10.0 or later) and clone-first (`git clone … ~/.claude-framework && bash ~/.claude-framework/install.sh`). | P1 | US2 |
| FR-008 | `docs/quickstart.md`, `docs/install.md` and `SETUP.md` each open with a one-line statement of their job and links to the others and to the per-OS pages. | P1 | US3 |
| FR-009 | `docs/install.md` keeps its §1–§7 numbering and every section a guard requires; inbound `install.md §N` citations still resolve to the same content. | P1 | US3 |
| FR-010 | `SETUP.md` keeps every step, check, command and rule; only cross-references change, and the allowlist-rule guard (`tests/smoke.sh:778-785`) stays green. SETUP.md is read through `curl`, so every new link in it is an absolute GitHub URL (`https://github.com/joaoariedi/hefesto/blob/main/docs/…`), not a relative path. | P1 | US3 |
| FR-011 | `docs/contributing.md` exists and covers: running the smoke suite (tier 1, `SMOKE_LIVE=1`, `node --test`), commit convention (subject hook-enforced; trailer a `git-workflow.md` rule), branch names, merge-commit convention (cited from the `human:merge` ancestry gate), review (`/hefesto:hef.review`, CI jobs, a person merges); each claim is traceable to a repo file. | P1 | US4 |
| FR-012 | `README.md` links `docs/contributing.md` from its contribute section. | P1 | US4 |
| FR-013 | The README presents single lane and four-or-more lanes with a choosing rule consistent with quick start §3, and points to quick start §5 and §6. | P2 | US5 |
| FR-014 | `docs/quickstart.pt-BR.md` mirrors the English quick start's sections, hand-overs, links and commands. | P2 | US6 |
| FR-015 | The quick-start guard in `tests/smoke.sh` is updated: the per-OS tool strings (`bubblewrap`, `brew install`) are required on the per-OS pages, and both quick starts must link all three per-OS pages; the six-section and step-count checks stay. | P1 | US2, US6 |
| FR-016 | A guard asserts the README stays under 150 lines and links `docs/contributing.md` and the three per-OS pages; it is mutation-tested (constitution 3). | P1 | US1, US4 |
| FR-017 | Every command in the changed docs is spelled `/hefesto:hef.<name>` (the namespace guard at `tests/smoke.sh:6436` stays green) and every new relative link resolves. | P1 | US1–US6 |

## Success Criteria

| ID | Criterion | Validation Method |
|----|-----------|-------------------|
| SC-001 | `wc -l README.md` < 150 | the new guard (FR-016) and a manual count |
| SC-002 | `tests/smoke.sh` tier 1 passes with zero failures, including doc counts, links, command spelling, quick-start and SETUP guards | run `tests/smoke.sh` |
| SC-003 | Each new guard goes red when its condition is broken (a README padded past 150 lines, the contributing link removed, `WSL` removed from the Windows page, `bubblewrap` removed from the Linux page, a per-OS link removed from a quick start) | in-suite: the guard is a function of a root, run on mutated temp copies by `tests/smoke.sh` itself |
| SC-007 | No doc cites a README section by number (`README §`) after the move | `grep -rn 'README §' docs/ SETUP.md` returns nothing |
| SC-004 | Every heading removed from `README.md` appears in the plan's destination table with a `docs/` target that contains the facts | review against the plan |
| SC-005 | `grep -rn 'bubblewrap socat' README.md docs/quickstart*.md docs/install.md` returns nothing; the per-OS pages contain them | grep |
| SC-006 | `git diff main -- SETUP.md` touches only cross-reference lines | diff review |

## Clarifications

No open markers. Every open point was decided from the code; the decisions and their evidence are listed
under "Decisions taken here". The item's owner answered the plan-review questions on 2026-11-07:

- **Q: Direction — README skeleton, three per-OS pages, `docs/contributing.md`, quick start and
  `install.md` reshaped?** A: Yes, this structure.
- **Q: Round 2 plan-review changes (six, `plan-review.md`)?** A: Apply all six, re-review once.
